items.note: General account of the Hindu temple: mandapas, solid Prasada, small dark cubical garbhagrha with plain walls, carvings ceasing at its door.
Temple has no facade; walls project in offsets giving a stepped, cross-shaped or star-shaped plan around the square garbhagrha.
Main images (parsva-devatas) in niches/ghanadvara nearer the centre; surrounding images (avarana-devatas) more exposed on the wall.
Figures on the Prasada walls form belts and vertical sequences, do not form compositions beyond a single buttress; ascent to the kumbha above the amalaka.
Temple body as 'body of God', likeness of Prakrti; circumambulation as the way the devotee comprehends the monument (interpretive reading).
Massive-door niches at cardinal points hold main aspects of the god; Ashtadikpalas indispensable; Nagas, Sardulas, Apsaras, Surasundaris, Mithunas on facets.

items.note: Treatment of garments, jewellery, headgear and coiffure of temple images; mukuta of greater gods adds height.
Stances of images: samabhanga, abhanga, tribhanga, atibhanga classification.
Footnote: the Samaranganasutradhara, LXXXII, 2-3 speaks of 11 rasas, adding Preyas and Pratyaksa to the usual nine. (old OCR / quoted via Kramrisch)
Iconometry: navatala (nine face lengths) as rule for gods' images, tala = 12 angulas; ten-tala for Brahma, Vishnu, Siva per Vaikhanasagama.
Rules of the proportion canons: trunk divided in three equal parts, face 12 angulas, Dasatala built on Navatala by adding angulas.
Indian image proportion is based on number with face length as module; modifications use the angula; crowns exceed face height.
Doorway of garbhagrha frames the image; Brhatsamhita proportions of the door (threshold, jambs, height twice width); guardian divinities at the bottom.
Door-jamb branches (sakha) 3, 5, 7 or 9 contribute to vertical mouldings.
Lotus carved at the centre of the threshold; none may tread on it.
River-goddesses, procreative couples, gana figures and creepers carved on the door-jambs.
River goddesses Ganga, Mandakini, Yamuna flanking the door; their presence acts as ablution and initiation at the entrance.
Door-way as iconostasis with mithuna, sardula and gana on each sakha.
Guardians of the threshold (dvarapalas) bear the weapons and fearful traits of the temple's god.
Vahana image faces the entrance, coaxial with the garbhagrha image; Nandin in mandapa directs the approach.
Four doors named Santi, Vidya, Nivrtti, Pratistha, with Saiva kala terminology.
Single real opening (entrance) repeated symbolically as ghanadvara niches; major niches hold images of the main divinity.
Gavaksa as Sukanasa antefix shielding the sikhara; on Nagara temples sikhara offsets covered by a web of gavaksas.
Footnote citing Samaranganasutradhara LVII on varieties of nasa (Surasena, Simhakarna). (old OCR / quoted via Kramrisch)
Interpretation of gavaksa as 'ray-wheel' or 'sun-arch'; windows closed, symbolic not functional.

items.note: Kirttimukha at apex of gavaksa, most prominent on sukanasa of Nagara temples.
Kirttimukha also on the threshold of the garbhagrha beside the lotus stalk and as grasa-pattika along the socle.
Description of the Kirttimukha: lion-like, horned, simha-mukha.
